title: Pinned Model API Compatibility Manifest and Eval Protocol
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Define a machine-readable compatibility manifest and an automated evaluation protocol that together guarantee backward-compatible behavior for pinned model versions (prompt shapes, output signatures, and parameter semantics). The manifest will be bundled with published performance snapshots and used to gate rollouts, CI checks, and runtime compatibility checks across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
background: Customers pin model versions and rely on stable IO and parameter semantics. Recent onboarding work revealed subtle regressions when model checkpoints change tokenization behavior, default sampling semantics, or structured-output delimiters. Existing tickets focus on policy and tests, but we lack a single canonical artifact and CI integration that: (1) declares the exact input/output contract for a pinned version, (2) publishes associated performance profile metadata, and (3) drives automated regression detection in the rollout pipeline.
proposed_solution:
1) Define a JSON manifest schema (compat_manifest.json) that specifies: canonical prompt shapes with example tokens, required and optional parameters with value domains and default semantics, structured-output schemas (JSON Schema or protobuf reference), and deprecation windows for parameter changes.
2) Publish a paired performance snapshot artifact that includes p50/p95 latency, token-cost curve by input length bucket, memory/kv-cache sizing, and supported quantization profiles.
3) Implement an evaluation harness that runs: unit-level deterministic shape checks, statistical semantic similarity tests over a curated prompt corpus, and token-level diffs for nondeterministic outputs.
4) Integrate CI gating: manifest + snapshot must be present to mark a model as pin-eligible; pipeline runs regression thresholds and blocks rollouts on violations.
5) Add server-side runtime guard that rejects requests incompatible with the pinned manifest (unknown parameter names, mismatched prompt shape) and returns a clear error with remediation suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: compat_manifest.json schema reviewed and merged in model-onboarding repo
Performance snapshot format defined and produced by the onboarding job
Automated eval harness executes in CI and produces pass/fail with detailed diffs
Rollout pipeline rejects new pinned-version artifact on regression above defined thresholds
Runtime guard in Hosted and Dedicated returns descriptive errors for manifest mismatches
Docs and quickstart for clients to read manifest and validate prompts locally
test_plan: Create 3 synthetic pinned model artifacts (simple, structured-json, chat) and author manifests
Run CI harness to validate that token-level diffs, schema conformance, and semantic similarity thresholds are computed and reported
Inject a deliberate regression (change delimiting token or default temperature) to verify CI blocking behavior
End-to-end canary: promote a pinned model to canary rollout, confirm runtime guard rejects invalid client requests
Run load test to ensure runtime guard and manifest parsing add <5% latency at p95
rollout_plan: Week 1: Spec review and manifest schema RFC with Applied ML and SDK owners
Week 2: Implement manifest generator in onboarding pipeline and performance snapshot exporter
Week 3: Build CI harness and evaluate against historical pinned artifacts
Week 4: Add runtime guard and feature flag behind canary for Hosted; enable for Dedicated on request
Week 5: Docs, SDK validation helpers, and cross-team training; flip feature flag for full enforcement pending metrics
notes: Manifest must be extensible; expect future fields for hardware hints and kv-cache layout metadata.
Evaluation harness should support pluggable semantic similarity backends (embeddings or house-built scorers).
Consider exposing a lightweight 'manifest-check' API for partners to validate before pinning.
